title: Does AI Help or Hurt Learning? Harvard Builds an Age-by-Age Guide
title_zh: 人工智能有助于还是有损学习？哈佛推出按年龄划分的指南
source_name: Education Week — “Harvard Taps 5,000 Studies to Show How AI Helps or Hinders Learning” (12 Nov 2026)
summary_zh: 据《教育周刊》11月12日报道，哈佛大学教育研究生院推出免费在线工具“AI Guidance by Age Matrix”（按年龄划分的人工智能使用指南），它汇集了涉及81个人类发展领域的5000多项研究。该工具属于11月10日启动的“Compass Collaborative”项目，目的是缩小发展科学的结论与教育者、决策者和科技公司在人工智能问题上的实际做法之间的差距。项目负责人认为，学习的基本规律没有变：人需要与更有经验的人建立紧密关系，并有足够机会练习技能。指南以9到11岁儿童为例，指出自适应平台和检查AI答案有助于学习，而直接给作业答案的工具可能妨碍记忆的形成。文章最后介绍了教师们褒贬不一的评价，以及哈佛把它作为“持续更新的资源”的计划。
paragraphs: How should children use artificial intelligence at school? Teachers and parents everywhere are asking this, and a new Harvard tool aims to help them answer it. On 12 November, Education Week reported that the Harvard Graduate School of Education has released the AI Guidance by Age Matrix, a free online resource that shows how AI may help or hinder learning. It is built on more than 5,000 pieces of research across 81 areas of human development.

The tool is part of Compass Collaborative, a new initiative launched on 10 November. Its goal is to close the gap between what developmental science says about how people learn and the decisions that educators, policymakers and technology companies are making about AI. According to its co-director Jeff Curley, schools are trying to deal with AI in very different ways, and much of this is being done without much evidence.

Research on AI in classrooms is still emerging, and the results so far are mixed. However, Tessa Forshaw, the other co-director, argues that some basic truths about learning have not changed. People learn best when they have close relationships with more experienced people and plenty of opportunities to practise the skills they are developing. If a use of AI moves learners towards practice or human relationships, it is generally a good sign. If it moves them away, it may be worth thinking twice.

Users of the website choose their role, such as teacher or parent, a developmental area like creativity or relationships, and an age range from early childhood to adulthood. Then they see a summary of what the research says, together with practical recommendations. For example, children aged 9 to 11 are still strengthening their working memory and attention. Adaptive platforms that keep tasks at the right level of difficulty may help them, and checking AI answers can train critical thinking. By contrast, tools that simply provide homework answers may short-circuit the process of recalling information, which is how memory is built.

Not every educator is convinced. A special education teacher in Michigan called the tool a helpful deep dive into the stages of children's development, while an assistant principal in Nevada said it still feels basic and that he would not recommend it yet. Harvard says the matrix will be a "living resource", updated as new studies are published, because educators and parents are making decisions about AI in real time.
paragraphs_zh: 孩子在学校应该如何使用人工智能？各地的老师和家长都在问这个问题，而哈佛推出的一款新工具正是为了帮助他们找到答案。据《教育周刊》11月12日报道，哈佛大学教育研究生院发布了“按年龄划分的人工智能指南矩阵”（AI Guidance by Age Matrix）。这是一个免费的在线资源，展示人工智能可能如何促进或阻碍学习。它建立在5000多项研究的基础上，这些研究涵盖人类发展的81个领域。
这款工具是11月10日启动的新项目“Compass Collaborative”的一部分。该项目的目标是缩小两者之间的差距：一边是发展科学对人们如何学习的结论，另一边是教育工作者、政策制定者和科技公司在人工智能问题上正在做出的决定。该项目的联合负责人杰夫·柯利表示，各个学校应对人工智能的方式大相径庭，而其中很多做法都缺乏充分的证据支持。
关于课堂中人工智能的研究仍处于起步阶段，目前的结果好坏参半。不过，另一位联合负责人泰莎·福肖认为，学习的一些基本规律并没有改变：当人们与更有经验的人建立紧密的关系，并且有大量机会练习自己正在培养的技能时，学习效果最好。如果某种人工智能的用法能让学习者更多地练习或更多地接触人际关系，那通常是个好兆头；如果它让学习者远离这些，那就值得三思。

使用这个网站时，用户先选择自己的身份（例如老师或家长）、一个发展领域（例如创造力或人际关系），以及一个年龄段（从幼儿期到成年期）。随后，网站会显示研究结论的概要以及实用的建议。例如，9到11岁的孩子仍在增强他们的工作记忆和注意力。能把任务保持在合适难度的自适应平台可能对他们有帮助，而检查人工智能给出的答案可以锻炼批判性思维。相比之下，直接提供作业答案的工具可能会让孩子跳过回忆信息的过程，而记忆正是通过这一过程形成的。
并不是每位教育工作者都认可这款工具。密歇根州的一位特殊教育教师称，它对儿童发展的各个阶段做了很有帮助的深入探讨；而内华达州的一位副校长则表示，这个工具目前仍然显得比较简单，他暂时不会推荐使用。哈佛表示，这个矩阵将是一个“持续更新的资源”，会随着新研究的发表而更新，因为教育工作者和家长们此刻就在为人工智能的使用做决定。

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A study proving that AI always improves students' test scores.
A new Harvard tool that gives age-based advice on how AI may affect learning.
A decision by US schools to ban AI homework tools.
A survey of parents' opinions about technology companies.
questions.explanation: 第一段介绍哈佛推出的按年龄划分的人工智能指南，后文都围绕它的目的、原则、用法和评价展开；文章没有说AI总能提高成绩，也没有提到禁令或家长调查。

evidence.quote: the Harvard Graduate School of Education has released the AI Guidance by Age Matrix, a free online resource that shows how AI may help or hinder learning

questions.prompt: According to the guidance, how might tools that simply provide homework answers affect children aged 9 to 11?
options: They may stop children from practising recall, which builds memory.
They may strengthen children's working memory.
They may keep tasks at the right level of difficulty.
They may improve children's relationships with teachers.
questions.explanation: 第四段说直接给作业答案的工具可能让孩子跳过回忆信息的过程，而记忆正是靠这个过程形成的。保持合适难度的是自适应平台，不是答案工具。

evidence.quote: By contrast, tools that simply provide homework answers may short-circuit the process of recalling information, which is how memory is built.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about the AI Guidance by Age Matrix?
options: It is the final answer to every question about AI in schools.
Every teacher who has tried it has praised it.
It is expected to change as more research becomes available.
It is designed only for university researchers.
questions.explanation: 最后一段说它是“持续更新的资源”，会随新研究发表而更新，可推断它并非最终定论，而会不断变化。文中有副校长不推荐，所以不是人人称赞；用户也包括老师和家长。

evidence.quote: Harvard says the matrix will be a "living resource", updated as new studies are published
